history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: This temple is already recorded = seq 992 (id neelakanteshwara-temple-nizamabad, name "Sri Neelakanteshwara Temple"); keep-or-drop/merge decision needed for a duplicates pair. Identity confirmed: the ancient Neelakanteshwara Shiva temple at Kanteshwar locality in Nizamabad city, dedicated to Shiva as Neelakanteshwara (the blue-throated lord). The temple is famous for its Nagara-style architecture with carved walls and pillars. Local tradition, supported by a stone inscription cited by sources, attributes construction to the Satavahana king Satakarni II; trawell's history says it was built for the Jains and converted to a Shiva temple in the Kakatiya period. DATE FLAG: Satavahanas ruled in the 2nd c. BCE-3rd c. CE, so the simultaneous claims 'Satakarni II built it' and 'about 500 years old' are internally inconsistent - treat all dates as unverified. Special feature: on Rathasaptami day, sun rays fall directly on the Shiva linga.

name: Kanteshwar Temple
town_description: Kanteshwar is a locality within Nizamabad city, Telangana, on Armoor Road; the temple lies about 2.2 km from Nizamabad bus station.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~180 km).
travel.road: Within Nizamabad city at Kanteshwar; cab or auto from the bus/railway stations.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; visit on Rathasaptami (Jan/Feb) or Shivaratri for the main festivals.
